# LLM gate runs record no per-run request or tool-call counts, so the gates cannot be tuned

## The gap

**Nothing durably records how many model requests or tool calls a gate run consumed.** There is no
usage log on disk, and the audit sidecar carries criteria and citations but no request/tool-call
counts. Established while investigating rebar ticket c827: the control-group question
"how many of the 240 available requests did the epics that closed cleanly actually use?" **could not
be answered from the store at all.**

## Why this matters — it is why the same bug recurred six times

The completion gate's step budget has been raised **five times** across its history
(the history sweep on rebar ticket c827), a hard tool-call cap was proposed and deferred
(rebar ticket 7c58) then proposed and rejected (rebar ticket b2bb), and the verifier's own creating
epic was force-closed citing the limitation as "documented". **Every one of those decisions was made
without spend data**, because the data was never recorded.

The cost of that absence is measurable: answering a single question about this gate required **four
live instrumented runs at ~20-50 minutes each**, re-deriving numbers that should have been a query.
And the tuning advice the docs give (the loop-tuning advice in `docs/llm-framework.md`'s completion-verifier
section — "a high recursion limit means you're paying for a loop, fix the loop") is unactionable, because nothing tells an operator whether
they are paying for a loop or for breadth.

This is the same **"computed then discarded"** shape as two sibling defects: the repetition
diagnostic that `interpret_failure` builds and `raise_completion_workflow_failure` drops
(rebar ticket c827), and the deterministic child-closure proof collapsed to a boolean
(rebar ticket 6ec8). The value is produced and thrown away one frame from the surface.

## Scope note

`usage_log` machinery already exists in-tree (e.g. `usage_log.failure_usage`,
`usage_log.capture_attempt_messages`), and `RunContext` exposes `.usage` inside the tool-filter predicate (`agent_call.py:70-71`), though that predicate currently reads only `run_ctx.run_step` — the usage actually reachable at record time comes from `failure_usage`, not from that predicate.
**Establish what is already captured before adding anything** — the likely defect is that the data is
captured and not persisted, in which case this is a wiring job, not new accounting. Do not build a
second, parallel usage mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

Each line is one independently verifiable deliverable.

- [ ] a gate run persists the model requests it consumed
- [ ] a gate run persists the tool calls it consumed
- [ ] a gate run persists the `request_limit` it ran under
- [ ] a gate run persists the `tool_calls_limit` it ran under
- [ ] a gate run persists the step name
- [ ] a gate run persists the ticket id when the caller supplies one
- [ ] a gate run persists wall-clock duration
- [ ] the FAILURE path records all of the above (a run that exhausts its budget or errors is
      exactly when the numbers are needed, and is the case most likely to be missed)
- [ ] the SUCCESS path records all of the above, so a clean run is usable as a control group
- [ ] the distinct-vs-total tool-call-signature counts are recorded, so a LOOP is distinguishable
      from genuine BREADTH after the fact without re-running
- [ ] a gate run persists the worst-consecutive-repeat count
- [ ] a gate run persists `finish_reason`, recorded for triage but deliberately not rendered
- [ ] the record is produced by an ordinary gate run with no env var set
- [ ] the record is produced with no instrumentation added to the run
- [ ] the named retrieval command RENDERS the total tool-call count in its own output
- [ ] the named retrieval command RENDERS the distinct tool-call count in its own output
- [ ] that rendering is proven by pasting the rendered output, never a raw JSONL line
- [ ] the retrieval command's existing token/cost table is unchanged, pinned by a test
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` points operators at the new rendered command output
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` documents the new `.rebar/usage.jsonl` artifact
- [ ] a test pins that the counts are WRITTEN on the success path
- [ ] a test pins that the counts are WRITTEN on the exhaustion path
- [ ] a test pins that a gate run writes with NO env var set (the positive gate-sink case)
- [ ] a test pins that a NON-gate run still writes nothing with no env var set (the control)
- [ ] no second parallel usage mechanism is introduced where the existing one can be wired

### Explicitly OUT of scope (recorded so it is not mistaken for a gap)

**The record carries WHOLE-RUN aggregates only.** It does NOT carry the ordered tool-call
signature SEQUENCE. The windowed distinct-ratio that rebar ticket 70bc establishes is a
trailing-window set cardinality, which provably needs that ordered sequence, so it is NOT
computable from this record — only the whole-run ratio is. That whole-run ratio does reproduce
every measured example (238/258 = 0.92 healthy; 76/257 = 0.30, 167/270 = 0.62, 135/264 = 0.51
pathological), which is the discrimination this ticket needs. Storing the sequence would grow
each row without bound, so if 70bc pins a window size the natural follow-up is to emit per-window
ratios at that size from the same `_repetition_summary` seam. Flagged for 70bc, not done here.

**`finish_reason` is a raw provider passthrough with no vocabulary owned by rebar.** It is
recorded for triage (it is what distinguishes a length-stop from a tool-stop when reading a
failed row) and is deliberately NOT rendered by the retrieval command, precisely because its
value set is the provider's and would otherwise read as a rebar-defined enum.

## Fix plan — wire the EXISTING mechanism, add nothing parallel

Root cause (confirmed at runtime; full RCA in the first comment): `usage_log.record()` builds its
row from the single allowlist `_FIELDS` (`usage_log.py:32`, iterated at `:311`), so the seven
further keys `failure_usage()` (`usage_log.py:136-191`) already computes — `tool_calls`,
`tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`, `request_limit`,
`tool_calls_limit`, `finish_reason` — are **computed and then discarded at the write**.

### Step 1 — `record()` stops discarding, and two NEW names are introduced

All three of the following are NEW work; none exists in the tree today:

- **`_SHAPE_FIELDS`** (new module constant) — a second explicit allowlist holding those seven
  keys, written by `record()` **only when present** in the `usage` dict. Absent means "not
  measured"; defaulting to `0` would make a shapeless caller assert the falsehood "this run used
  no tools", which later aggregates would sum as fact. An explicit allowlist, not `**usage`
  passthrough, so this module keeps owning its durable schema.
- **`run_shape`** (new module-level ALIAS) — `run_shape = failure_usage`. A thin outcome-neutral
  name for the EXISTING reducer, introduced because the success path now calls the same function
  and a success-path call spelled `failure_usage(...)` would tell a reader the opposite of the
  truth. `failure_usage` is NOT renamed: it has live call sites in `llm/structured_run.py` that
  another agent is editing concurrently, so renaming would collide.
- **`shape_only(shape)`** (new function) — returns exactly the `_SHAPE_FIELDS` subset of a
  `run_shape` result. It exists so a caller merging the shape into its own usage dict need not
  reach into the private field tuple, and so the token totals the reducer also computes are
  dropped rather than overwriting the provider's authoritative figures.

`record()` also gains `duration_s` and `ticket` as explicit optional keyword arguments.

### Step 2 — the SUCCESS path, field by field

`record_call_spend` (`agent_call.py`) receives neither the limits nor the call start time, so the
plumbing is stated explicitly rather than left implicit. **The reducer is called in `runner.py`,
NOT inside `record_call_spend`** — the runner is the frame that holds all three missing inputs:

- `runner.py`, on the success path, calls
  `usage_log.run_shape(run_messages, request_limit=req_limit, tool_calls_limit=max(8, eff_max_iter))`.
  `req_limit` and `eff_max_iter` are already locals there (from `build_usage_limits`), and
  `run_messages` is already populated on the success path because `capture_attempt_messages`
  extends the sink from its `finally`, not from an `except` (verified at runtime).
- **`request_limit` / `tool_calls_limit` reach the row because they are ARGUMENTS to that call
  and the reducer echoes them into its own result** — that is the whole mechanism, and it is why
  no new parameter is needed on `record_call_spend` for them.
- `usage_log.shape_only(...)` filters that result to `_SHAPE_FIELDS`, which `runner.py` merges
  into `usage`. Deliberately NOT the reducer's token totals: those are message-derived
  approximations and must never overwrite `_extract_usage`'s authoritative provider figures.
- **`duration_s`** — computed in `runner.py` as `time.monotonic() - _t0` (the existing call-start
  marker) and passed as a NEW optional kwarg on `record_call_spend`, which forwards it to
  `record`.
- **`ticket`** — `req.target.get("ticket_id")`, passed the same way. Absent when the caller set no
  target, and then omitted from the row.
- The failure path passes `duration_s`/`ticket` through `record_failure` as keyword-only
  arguments with defaults, leaving its existing positional signature unbroken.
- BOTH paths are wrapped in a swallow-and-log guard, not only the success one: telemetry must
  never break the call it measures. On the success path `runner.py` wraps the shape capture; on
  the FAILURE path `record_failure` already wraps its ENTIRE body — shape capture, the
  `duration_s`/`ticket` forwarding, and the `record()` write alike — and that is load-bearing
  there, because its caller is an `except` block whose one job is to re-raise the provider's
  exception unchanged: an error escaping telemetry would REPLACE that exception and destroy the
  real diagnosis.

### Step 3 — gate runs record with no env var set, and WHERE the root comes from

`record()` resolves its sink through a new `_resolve_sink()`: `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` (explicit, still
wins) -> else, **iff `in_gate_session()`**, `<repo root>/.rebar/usage.jsonl` when that directory
already exists -> else no-op exactly as today.

**The repo root is obtained by a new `_repo_root_for_default_sink()`, which calls
`rebar.config.repo_root()` — the git toplevel of the PROCESS CWD.** This is deliberately NOT the
gate's active code root. In attested mode `gate_read_root` points the code root at a throwaway
temp snapshot; writing the usage log there would produce a record that vanishes with the
snapshot and is unretrievable from the operator's checkout. Resolving from CWD instead puts the
row in the checkout the operator is standing in, which is the only place they can read it from.
Verified empirically: a real attested `review-plan` wrote its rows to the working checkout's
`.rebar/usage.jsonl`, not into a snapshot dir.

`in_gate_session()` is the existing fail-closed marker every code-reading gate binds through the
single chokepoint `gate_source.gate_read_root` (`gate_source.py:110`, entered by
`plan_review/__init__.py:459` and `completion.py:485`), so this needs no new plumbing. Imported
via `rebar.llm.config`, not `gate_context` directly, because `test_gate_context_seam.py` forbids
the latter for every module under `src/`. Every non-gate caller stays byte-identical, preserving
the module's no-op-when-unset guarantee.

**Lifecycle of the new artifact.** `.rebar/usage.jsonl` is append-only, git-ignored, disposable
local state: rebar never reads it back (only the operator and `summarize` do), so it may be
truncated or deleted at any time with no loss of function. Nothing prunes it, so it grows with
every gate run; the documented guidance is to delete it after a measurement, or point
`REBAR_USAGE_LOG` at a per-session path for a clean window. No rotation is implemented, matching
the existing caveat already recorded for the long-lived review-bot sink in
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:200-211`. Each row is one single-append complete line, so
concurrent gate runs interleave rows without corrupting one.

### Step 4 — the retrieval command must RENDER the new fields

`summarize()` today folds only the token `_FIELDS`, so a row can carry `tool_calls=125,
tool_calls_distinct=1` and the operator running the named command still sees only token counters.
**A fix that leaves the signal written but not displayed reproduces the very "computed then
discarded" pattern this ticket exists to remove, one layer further out.** So a new
`_run_shape_section()` helper renders a `Run shape (loop vs breadth)` table — per op: calls,
total tool calls, distinct, the distinct/total ratio, worst consecutive repeat, and both limits.
An op that made no tool calls prints an em dash, never `0.000`, because no measurement is not a
perfect loop.

Constraint: the existing token/cost table is **unchanged** and the new section is APPENDED, never
merged in as extra columns — that table feeds `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on the two billable weekly
jobs and several existing tests assert on it. Rows carrying no shape fields (every pre-aec1 row)
are skipped, and an all-shapeless log renders no section at all, so old logs summarize exactly as
they did.

### Step 5 — documentation

`docs/llm-framework.md` is updated in the same change: the `usage_log` section documents the
run-shape fields, `duration_s`/`ticket`, the default gate sink and its lifecycle, and shows the
rendered `Run shape` table with both poles. This is what makes the existing tuning advice at
the loop-tuning advice in `docs/llm-framework.md` ("a high recursion limit means you're paying for a loop, fix the
loop") actionable for the first time — that advice is the motivation for this ticket, so leaving
it without a pointer to the new output would leave the motivating gap open.

## Retrieval

    python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl

## Testing

    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q
    make lint && make typecheck

`tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py` drives the REAL runner offline (`FunctionModel` +
`ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS=False`, the established pattern in `test_usage_log_failed_calls.py`) and
reads the written FILE, varying the path axis three ways: `_ok_model` (success), `_breadth_model`
(all-distinct exploration, terminates), `_looping_model` (one repeated signature, runs to budget
exhaustion). Named tests:

- exhaustion path: `tool_calls`, `request_limit`, `tool_calls_limit` are written
- success path: `tool_calls`/`tool_calls_distinct` are written, and a SEPARATE test asserts
  `request_limit`, `tool_calls_limit` and `duration_s` are present, so the Step-2 plumbing cannot
  silently regress to failure-path-only
- the recorded distinct-vs-total ratio separates a loop from breadth FROM THE RECORD ALONE
- POSITIVE gate-sink case: a gate run writes with no env var set (the `.rebar` root is pinned via
  `_repo_root_for_default_sink` so the test needs no chdir)
- CONTROL: a NON-gate run still writes nothing with the env var unset, so the positive test above
  cannot pass for the trivial reason that everything writes
- rendering: `summarize()` output CONTAINS the tool-call and distinct counts and reads as a loop
- invariance: the existing token/cost table is unchanged, and a pre-aec1 log with no shape fields
  renders with no run-shape section at all
